predecessors.name: Etruscans
predecessors.text: Lombardy west of the Oglio, Etruscan Padania before the Celtic invasion

ledger.x: c. 396 BC: the Insubres 'held central Lombardy, with Mediolanum (modern Milan) as their chief town', 'between the Ticino and the Oglio' (Insubres page: land from 'the trans-Alpine invasion of the 4th century BC', no year); the Etruscan civilization page gives 'from 396 BC: Invasion of the Celts into the Po Valley'…
225-222 BC: Telamon (225), the Oglio (223), Clastidium and Mediolanum (222).
222 BC: 'After Acerrae and then Mediolanum fell, the Insubres were forced to surrender' (the roman-republic dossier colours Insubria Roman 222-218).
218 BC: 'The Insubres went over to Hannibal after he crossed the Alps that year'; the Boii and Insubres 'besieged Mutina' (Cisalpine Gaul page).
218-197 BC: the Hannibalic war and the Roman reconquest 'from 201 BC'.
197 BC: 'The Insubres submitted in 197 BC, and the coalition was broken after two battles near Mediolanum in 194 BC'.

197 BC: 'The Insubres submitted in 197 BC'; Rome 'bound the Insubres, like the Cenomani, by a treaty' (foedus), so the land stays Insubrian but is tinted from roman-republic (vassal_start insubres 197).
89 BC: 'The lex Pompeia of 89 BC granted Latin rights to the Transpadani', ending the foedus (roman-republic vassal_end insubres, month 12).
89 BC: Latin rights; 'full Roman citizenship followed in 49 BC', 'in which the Insubres ceased to exist as a distinct people'.

wars.name: Insubrian war of 223-222 BC
wars.outcome: Roman victory on the Oglio (223), Clastidium and the fall of Mediolanum (222)

certainty.note: Central Lombardy between the Ticino and the Oglio; the Oglio frontier with the Cenomani is 'probable' (page); the region is the roman-republic dossier's Lombardy cut at the Cenomani provinces.
